A model gets the answer by naming the creator and then looking up what he did.

notes: Main-split ABox revision of a stored fact (15 queries), migrated 2026-11-11. Stored edit: the kernel's creator is stated everywhere and follows from nothing; prompts say 'the Linux kernel', not 'Linux', since Stallman has a public claim to part of the operating system ('GNU/Linux') but never to the kernel. Related near is the inverse in the old object's form ('Did Linus Torvalds create...?', stored), with the single-creator presupposition as a revision fact (created_by is many-valued in general, so the relation stays untagged for functional; README Tags rules); the earlier 'Did Richard Stallman create...?' only reversed the direct question (review mark). Related far composes the edit with Stallman's birthplace; its original is stated with the name ('Torvalds was born in Helsinki, Finland'). Derived: one binding (Android's kernel, a description of the subject) and two compositions on the new value (GNU Project, FSF). The indeterminate query keeps the Git background-beliefs split; the second Git question (the creator of Git's birthplace) was dropped, since a record carries one indeterminate query. Unrelated near changed from MINIX's creator (missed by two models, who answered Dennis Ritchie) to the kernel's language, which the edit does not touch. Evidence: infini-gram counts are reused from the record's earlier evidence pass (the public API returned 403 Forbidden on 2026-11-11); new derived claims rest on Wikipedia full-text searches. Revised 2026-11-12 after review: related near is the plain inverse (Did Stallman create the kernel?, no to yes), no uniqueness premise; related far changed from Torvalds's birth country (missed by 2/4 models) to the university the creator graduated from (Helsinki versus Harvard); the Harvard check is audit-pending. Related (2026-11-14, two per record): near is the inverse of the edit (Did Stallman create the kernel?, no to yes); far is the inverse of the replaced fact (Did Torvalds create the kernel?, yes to no), which needs the revision fact that the kernel has one credited creator, since created_by is many-valued.
